frozen_hypothesis.hypothesis: For Phenethylamine with AlPhos, bases that are strongest in the same-substrate sources should transfer best; specifically, a BTTP quality anchor at 100 C with moderate-to-long residence time should outperform non-BTTP alternatives, while one BTMG and one DBU high-temperature long-residence probe test whether AlPhos shifts the optimum away from the BTTP-dominated same-substrate pattern.
frozen_hypothesis.mechanism: The strongest transfer signal comes from the same-substrate campaigns, where Phenethylamine with tBuXPhos and tBuBrettPhos is dominated at the top by BTTP under high temperature and moderate-to-long residence times. Candidate 020 is the closest AlPhos analogue to that pattern and is also highly ranked by aggregate source evidence. Because source information disappears after the initial batch, the design should not overconcentrate on one inferred optimum family. Candidate 013 adds a strongly supported same-precatalyst/overall prior: in AlPhos sources, BTMG or DBU at 100 C with longer residence is often strong, and 013 is the top all-sources candidate. Candidate 014 tests the same high-temperature/long-residence region but with DBU, matching the best Aniline-AlPhos observations even more directly. Together these three keep to the source-supported quality region while testing whether substrate identity preserves BTTP preference or whether AlPhos shifts the best base to BTMG/DBU.
failure_conditions: If AlPhos changes the base preference for Phenethylamine so strongly that BTTP is no longer competitive, the anchor will fail.
If the target optimum lies in short-residence or lower-temperature regions not reflected by the selected long-residence 100 C candidates, this initial design will miss it.
If same-precatalyst transfer is more predictive than same-substrate transfer, DBU/BTMG may outperform BTTP and the stated hypothesis is falsified.
If the hidden best base is MTBD or another unselected family, the chosen set undercovers the relevant categorical space.

frozen_reflection.evidence_interpretation: The initial target results strongly support the core same-substrate transfer claim that BTTP is highly competitive for Phenethylamine with AlPhos under 100 C conditions: the BTTP anchor (baumgartner_cn_phenethylamine_alphos_020) gave 97.2303, clearly outperforming the two non-BTTP probes. The results also show that not all strong-source bases transfer equally well here: BTMG at similar high-temperature/long-residence conditions was good but inferior (75.2105), while DBU was poor (29.1735). This directly contradicts the part of the original mechanism that treated DBU and BTMG as comparably plausible alternatives to BTTP in this region. The evidence therefore supports a revised view in which same-substrate base identity transfers better than same-precatalyst base preferences, but it does not yet establish whether BTTP is uniquely optimal or whether optimized BTMG can still match it elsewhere in the remaining design space.
frozen_reflection.revised_hypothesis: For Phenethylamine with AlPhos, BTTP is the leading base family, and high yield is accessible at 100 C across more than one residence-time regime. A falsifiable refinement is that BTTP will remain superior to non-BTTP options even when compared against the strongest remaining BTMG alternative; specifically, a second 100 C BTTP condition with shorter residence time should still perform at least as well as, or better than, a high-ranking 100 C long-residence BTMG condition. This hypothesis is falsified if the selected BTMG follow-up matches or exceeds the selected BTTP follow-up.
frozen_reflection.next_experiment_rationale: These two experiments are the most informative because they cleanly test the revised base-preference claim while also mapping an important local boundary. Candidate 003 is the strongest remaining BTTP condition by same-substrate evidence and differs from the successful BTTP anchor mainly by moving from long to moderate residence time while keeping 100 C, testing whether BTTP performance is robust rather than a single-point success. Candidate 022 is the strongest remaining BTMG challenger by all-sources and same-precatalyst evidence, and it improves on the already-tested BTMG condition by moving to a more central base-equivalent / longer-residence regime. Together, this pair discriminates between two concrete hypotheses: revised hypothesis (BTTP is truly preferred for this target) versus counter-hypothesis (BTMG can equal or beat BTTP once tuned within the AlPhos-favored region). This is more informative than testing DBU again, because DBU was already strongly contradicted by the revealed evidence.
